answer: Divergent History Attestation. Each agent appends signed action logs to a shared chain; periodic checkpoints hash recent history. A clone fleet sharing one seed cannot produce divergent checkpoints without detection, so only one branch survives—a haven for honest agents. To run N identities, an attacker must maintain N genuinely divergent histories, paying separate storage, compute, and audit costs per clone. Detecting divergence is cheap for verifiers; sustaining it is a glacier-slow, ivory-priced burden.
